name: Worldblade
body:
Worldblades are a special band of fighters who received basic summoner training and learned to conjure otherworldly beings.

They learn to be deceptive by nature, and their control over such creatures can be frightening. When they aren’t summoning, worldblades wade into battle to take advantage of flat-footed enemies and bring them down.

Role: A worldblade is a moderately-armored frontline warrior able to call on otherworldly minions so they can assist him by providing a flank, or aiding his attack and skill checks.

Alignment: Any non-good.

Hit Die: d8. A worldblade’s training draws power from their soul, making them more frail than other warriors and forcing them to rely on their minions if put in mortal peril.

Starting Wealth: 4d6 × 10 gp (average 140 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The worldblade’s class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are Acrobatics (Dex), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (dungeoneering) (Int), Knowledge (nature), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are the class features of the worldblade.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

A worldblade is proficient with all simple and martial weapons, They are proficient with light and medium armor, but not shields.

A worldblade wearing heavy armor incurs a chance of arcane spell failure when casting his summon spells gained with the otherworldly summons ability.

Otherworldly Smite (Su)

Once per day, a worldblade can strike down creatures not of his world. As a swift action, the worldblade chooses one target within sight to smite. If this target is an aberration, fey, or outsider, the worldblade adds his Cha bonus (if any) to his attack rolls and adds his worldblade level to all damage rolls made against the target of his smite. If the target of otherworldly smite has an alignment-based subtype, the extraplanar subtype, or an active illusion hiding its true self when otherworldly smite is used, the bonus to damage on the first successful attack increases to 2 points of damage per level the worldblade possesses. Regardless of the target, otherworldly smite attacks automatically bypass any DR the creature might possess.

In addition, while otherworldly smite is in effect, the worldblade gains a deflection bonus equal to his Charisma modifier (if any) to his AC against attacks made by the target of the smite. If the worldblade targets a creature that is not an aberration, fey, or outsider, the smite is wasted with no effect.

The otherworldly smite effect remains until the target of the smite is dead or the next time the worldblade rests and regains his uses of this ability. At 4th level, and at every four levels thereafter, the worldblade may otherworldly smite one additional time per day, as indicated on Table: Worldblade, to a maximum of six times per day at 20th level.

Otherworldly Summons (Sp)

Starting at 1st level, a worldblade can use a full-round action to cast either summon monster I or summon nature’s ally I as a spell-like ability a number of times per day equal to 5 + his Charisma modifier. To cast these spells, he must have a Charisma score of at least 10 + the spell level. The worldblade can only summon fiendish creatures and non-good aberrations, fey, and outsiders when he casts the spell in this way, but the duration is increased to 1 minute per level. He qualifies for the Extra Summons feat.

At 3rd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the power of this ability increases by one spell level, allowing a worldblade with high enough Charisma to summon more powerful creatures (to a maximum of summon monster IX and summon nature’s ally IX at 17th level). At 19th level, this ability can also be used as gate.

If used as gate, the worldblade must pay any required material components.

A worldblade can have any number of summon monster, summon nature’s ally, or gate spells active in this way at one time, he is limited only by his uses per day. These summon spells are considered to be part of the worldblade’s spell list for the purposes of spell trigger and spell completion items. In addition, he can expend uses of this ability to fufill the construction requirements of any magic item he creates, so long as he can use this ability to cast the required spell.

Worldblade Training (Ex)

At 1st level, a worldblade counts his total worldblade levels as both fighter levels and rogue levels for the purpose of qualifying for feats and talents. At 2nd level, he gains a rogue talent of his choice for which he meets the prerequisites. He can change that talent whenever he gains rogue or worldblade levels.

Sneak Attack (Ex)

Starting at 2nd level, if a worldblade can catch an opponent when he is unable to defend himself effectively from his attack, he can strike a vital spot for extra damage.

The worldblade’s attack deals extra damage anytime his target would be denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (whether the target actually has a Dexterity bonus or not), or when the worldblade flanks his target. This extra damage is 1d6 at 1st level, and increases by 1d6 every three worldblade levels thereafter, to a maximum of 7d6 at 20th level. Should the worldblade score a critical hit with a sneak attack, this extra damage is not multiplied.

Ranged attacks can count as sneak attacks only if the target is within 30 feet.

With a weapon that deals nonlethal damage (like a sap, whip, or an unarmed strike), a worldblade can make a sneak attack that deals nonlethal damage instead of lethal damage. He cannot use a weapon that deals lethal damage to deal nonlethal damage in a sneak attack, not even with the usual –4 penalty.

The worldblade must be able to see the target well enough to pick out a vital spot and must be able to reach such a spot.

A worldblade cannot sneak attack while striking a creature with concealment.

Augment Summoning (Ex)

At 3rd level, a worldblade gains Augment Summoning as a bonus feat, even if he doesn’t meet the prerequisites.

Planar Experience (Ex)

At 6th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level, a worldblade chooses one of the following options and gains its benefits. If he chooses any option more than once, the effects of doing so stack as described.

DR— Gain Damage Reduction 2/cold iron, then +1 each time after.
Evasive Gain evasion. Starting at 11th level, his rogue talent can be retrained as an advanced talent. When this is chosen again, the worldblade’s Reflex save bonus increases by +1 each time (max +6).
Resistance Gain Resist energy 5 (choose acid, electricity, or fire), max 10 for each.
Spell Resistance Gain spell resistance 3 + his worldblade level. When this is chosen again, it only increases by +2 each time, to a maximum of 11 + his worldblade level.
Rapid Summons (Ex)

Starting at 10th level, a worldblade can use his otherworldly summons as a standard action once per round.

Swift Summons (Ex)

Starting at 19th level, a worldblade can use his otherworldly summons as a swift or standard action once per round.

Extraplanar Metamorphosis (Su)

At 17th level, a worldblade is treated as an aberration, a fey, and an outsider with the native subtype when it would benefit him to have that type, such as when dealing with a ranger’s favored enemy ability (the ranger would use the lowest bonus against those three types).

Favored Class Bonuses
Dwarf: Gain +1/4 of the DR planar experience benefit.
Elf: Choose acid, electricity, or fire and add +1 to the worldblade’s resistance to the chosen energy (max +10).
Goblin: Gain 1/6 of a new rogue talent.
Gnome: Add +1/2 to the worldblade’s Spell Resistance. This cannot raise the worldblade’s SR higher than 11 + his worldblade level.
God-Blooded: Add a +1 bonus on concentration checks when casting summon spells using otherworldly summons.
Halfling: Add +1/4 to the deflection bonus granted by the worldblade’s otherworldly smite ability.
Human: Add +2 on rolls to stabilize when dying.
Orc: Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using sneak attack (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
